digest.headline: The Federal Reserve prepared its interest rate decision while Yardeni cut the S&P 500 target to 7,900.

lede.b: The Federal Reserve, which is the central bank of the United States that manages the country's money supply and interest rates, got ready to announce its next interest rate move. Treasury yields, which are the interest rates paid by the government when it borrows money from investors, edged down a little bit before the announcement. At the same time, an analyst named Yardeni lowered his target for the S&P 500 stock index to 7,900. This drop happened because rising yields across fixed-income markets mean that fewer companies in the index pay a dividend yield above 4%. Higher yields increase the opportunity cost, which is the loss of potential gain from other options when one alternative is chosen, of holding equities.
lede.i: The Federal Reserve prepared for its interest rate announcement as US Treasury yields edged down slightly. Market participants positioned themselves for the central bank's next move while broad equity indices adjusted. Yardeni cut the S&P 500 target to 7,900 following rising yields across fixed-income markets. Fewer companies in the index now yield over 4%, altering the opportunity cost of holding shares.
lede.a: The Federal Reserve readied its rate decision against a backdrop of marginally softer Treasury yields as market participants squared positions. Yardeni revised the S&P 500 target down to 7,900, citing rising fixed-income yields. The contraction in constituents yielding over 4% shifts the relative opportunity cost for equity holders.

items.b: The Federal Reserve prepared for its interest rate announcement as Treasury yields dropped slightly.
items.i: The Federal Reserve prepared its interest rate decision while Treasury yields edged down.
items.a: The Federal Reserve approached its rate announcement amid softer Treasury yields.

items.b: The King and Chancellor appointed three new non-executive directors to the Bank of England's supervisory board, and UK inflation climbed to 3.1%.
items.i: The Bank of England added three non-executive directors to its Court of Directors, while UK inflation accelerated to 3.1%.
items.a: The Bank of England appointed three non-executive directors to its Court of Directors as UK inflation reached 3.1%.

items.b: European equities went up and Daimler Truck shares gained support while German exports to Iraq reached $669m over six months.
items.i: European equities and Daimler Truck shares advanced as German export volumes to Iraq reached $669m over six months.
items.a: European equities advanced alongside Daimler Truck shares while German exports to Iraq totaled $669m over a six-month period.

items.b: The Nikkei index rose after energy shares gained, the USD/JPY currency pair tested the ¥156 resistance level, and Komatsu completed a 7.8 billion yen share buyback.
items.i: The Nikkei rose on energy sector gains to break a four-session losing streak, the USD/JPY pair tested ¥156, and Komatsu finished a 7.8 billion yen buyback.
items.a: The Nikkei snapped a four-session losing streak on energy gains, USD/JPY tested the ¥156 resistance level, and Komatsu completed a 7.8 billion yen share buyback.

thread.b: Central banks and interest rates drove market focus across multiple countries today. Central banks in the United States and Japan faced upcoming rate announcements. Meanwhile, inflation data shifted in the United Kingdom and Nigeria.
thread.i: Central bank policy expectations anchored cross-border trading as monetary authorities prepared rate decisions. Fixed-income yields and inflation prints influenced equity targets and currency pairs.
thread.a: Central bank policy anticipation dominated cross-border flows as market participants positioned ahead of Federal Reserve and Bank of Japan decisions. Fixed-income yield movements simultaneously drove equity index revisions and currency testing.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Federal Reserve rate decision and S&P 500 target cuts

stories.b: The Federal Reserve is the central bank of the United States. This is the government group that sets borrowing costs for the whole economy. It is about to announce its latest interest rate decision. Market watchers expect a rate hike today. Treasury yields edged down while awaiting the news.
stories.i: The Federal Reserve prepares to announce its interest rate decision. Market participants broadly expect a hike. Treasury yields edged down slightly ahead of the announcement. This comes as traders position themselves for the central bank's next move.
stories.a: The Federal Reserve approaches its rate announcement with a hike widely priced in by market participants. Treasury yields edged down in pre-announcement positioning. The implied path of future policy hinges on the tone of the accompanying statement regarding persistent inflation pressures.

stories.b: Yardeni cut the S&P 500 stock index target to 7,900. An index is a group of stocks tracked together to measure market health. This reduction happened because yields are rising. Rising yields make bonds pay more, which can draw money away from stocks. Fewer and fewer stocks in the index now yield over 4%.
stories.i: Yardeni cut the S&P 500 target to 7,900. The adjustment follows rising yields across fixed income markets. Fewer and fewer companies in the index now yield over 4%. Higher yields increase the opportunity cost of holding equities.
stories.a: Yardeni reduced the S&P 500 target to 7,900 driven by rising yields. The narrowing pool of index constituents yielding above 4% reflects compressed equity risk premiums. Higher discount rates continue to challenge equity valuations across the broader benchmark.

politics.b: Government officials watched economic data as the Federal Reserve prepared its choice. Lawmakers monitored how workers aged 55 and older left the workforce. The S&P 500 rose nearly 40% in two years during this demographic shift.
politics.i: Federal policy officials monitored financial conditions ahead of the central bank decision. Lawmakers observed demographic shifts as the workforce rate for individuals aged 55 and older shrank. The S&P 500 rose nearly 40% over a two-year period amidst these labor changes.
politics.a: Policymakers evaluated macroeconomic indicators as monetary authorities neared their rate decision. The contraction of the 55 plus workforce participation rate coincided with a nearly 40% gain in the S&P 500 over a two-year window.

timeline: Federal Reserve prepares to announce its latest interest rate decision.
Yardeni cuts the S&P 500 target to 7,900 citing rising yields.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: Bank of England appointments and rising inflation

stories.t: New Appointments to Bank of England Court
stories.b: His Majesty the King and the Chancellor appointed three new non-executive directors to the Bank of England's Court of Directors. The Bank of England is the central bank for the entire United Kingdom. It sets interest rates and oversees the financial system. The Court of Directors acts like a corporate board, managing the institution's internal affairs.
stories.i: His Majesty the King and the Chancellor appointed three new non-executive directors to the Bank of England's Court of Directors. The Court functions as an internal supervisory board overseeing the central bank's administration and strategy. These governance roles sit separately from monetary policy committees.
stories.a: His Majesty the King and the Chancellor appointed three new non-executive directors to the Bank of England's Court of Directors. The appointments refresh the oversight body responsible for internal governance and strategic management. The governing board operates independently from the Monetary Policy Committee.

stories.b: UK inflation climbed to 3.1%. Inflation means the speed at which prices for everyday goods and services go up over time. Insurers in the country are feeling direct pressure from this higher price growth. Higher costs affect how much insurance companies pay out for claims.
stories.i: UK inflation climbed to 3.1%. This increase places direct margin pressure on domestic insurers. Higher consumer prices typically raise claims costs across the sector.
stories.a: UK inflation climbed to 3.1%. Insurers face severe earnings pressure as claims severity scales with price growth. This unexpected uptick complicates pricing models across the sector.

politics.b: The UK Government announced new leadership roles at the central bank while the country deals with rising prices.
politics.i: The Chancellor and the Crown named three non-executive directors to the Bank of England's Court amidst rising inflation prints.
politics.a: Executive oversight at the central bank shifted with three new appointments to the Court of Directors as inflation prints at 3.1%.

timeline: Chancellor announces three new non-executive directors for Bank of England Court.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German equities rise, Daimler Truck gains, and trade expands

stories.t: European Equities Rise and Daimler Truck Gains Support
stories.src: Yahoo Finance UK · ad-hoc-news.de · 24/7 Wall St.
stories.b: European stock markets go up as the price of oil stops going up. Stock markets are places where pieces of companies are bought and sold. A major German stock index called the DAX moves higher. At the same time, Daimler Truck shares receive backing from market analysts. Analysts are experts who study companies to see if their shares are worth buying.
stories.i: European equities advance as oil prices stabilise prior to a central bank meeting. The DAX index posts gains while inflation concerns linger in the background. Daimler Truck shares secure fresh analyst support while the broader index lags behind peers.
stories.a: European indices grind higher as crude stabilisation relieves cost pressures ahead of the Federal Reserve rate decision. Daimler Truck outperforms on specific desk upgrades while the DAX trades at a discount to regional benchmarks. Flow models suggest tactical rebalancing into cyclical industrials as macro cross-currents pause.

stories.b: German businesses sell goods abroad to international buyers. These outbound shipments to Iraq total $669m over a period of six months. This figure shows the total monetary value of products sent from Germany to that destination during the tracked timeframe.
stories.i: German export volumes to Iraq register $669m across a six-month period. Bilateral trade flows capture demand from the Iraqi market for German manufactured goods. This data point underscores ongoing commercial ties between the two regions.
stories.a: German export figures to Iraq print at $669m over six months, mapping specific bilateral trade corridors. External demand resilience provides a minor offset to domestic industrial headwinds. Customs data confirms sustained capital goods absorption in the destination market.

politics.b: Government officials and public commentators issue statements on economic pressures.
politics.i: Market participants monitor administrative commentary regarding incoming price shocks.
politics.a: Fiscal authorities assess structural risks as external price shocks threaten growth projections.

timeline: German export statistics to Iraq hit $669m for the six-month period.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Nikkei bounces on energy while the yen tests resistance

stories.t: Nikkei Rises as Energy Shares Gain
stories.b: The Nikkei index is a large list that tracks the value of top companies in Japan. Shares are small pieces of ownership in a business. The Nikkei closed higher after a push from the energy sector. This ended a four-session losing streak for the index.
stories.i: The Nikkei closed higher on energy sector gains. This upward move broke a four-session losing streak for the shares index.
stories.a: The Nikkei broke its four-session losing streak driven by sector rotation into energy. Price action on the index reflects short-term positioning shifts rather than a broader macro reassessment.

stories.b: The USD/JPY exchange rate shows how many Japanese yen you can buy with one US dollar. The pair tested the ¥156 resistance level. Resistance is a price point that a currency struggles to cross. Traders watched this level ahead of upcoming decisions from the Bank of Japan and the US Federal Reserve.
stories.i: The USD/JPY pair tested the ¥156 resistance level. Market participants focused on this technical barrier ahead of imminent central bank decisions from the Federal Reserve and the Bank of Japan.
stories.a: Spot USD/JPY probed the ¥156 resistance threshold. Implied volatility climbed as desks squared positions ahead of the concurrent Federal Reserve and Bank of Japan rate announcements.

stories.b: Komatsu is a major manufacturing firm in Japan. The company bought back some of its own shares from the open market. This share buyback cost a total of 7.8 billion yen. A buyback reduces the number of shares available to the public.
stories.i: Komatsu completed a share buyback totaling 7.8 billion yen. The corporate action reduced its publicly traded float.
stories.a: Komatsu finalized its capital return program via a 7.8 billion yen open-market share repurchase. The transaction absorbed existing float without altering fundamental operational guidance.

politics.b: The Bank of Japan prepares to push its policy rate to the highest level seen in 31 years. Central banks manage interest rates for an entire country. Higher rates make borrowing more expensive.
politics.i: The Bank of Japan prepared to hike its policy rate to a 31-year high. The monetary authority adjusted its stance despite external currency pressures.
politics.a: The Bank of Japan advanced preparations to elevate its policy rate to a 31-year peak. Terminal rate pricing faced scrutiny as officials weighed domestic wage data against persistent FX pass-through risks.

timeline: Komatsu completed a 7.8 billion yen share buyback.
The Nikkei snapped a four-session losing streak on energy gains.
USD/JPY tested ¥156 resistance ahead of central bank meetings.

China.label: China
China.sub: Corporate fundraises and investments across China

stories.t: Leapmotor Secures Regulatory Clearance For Private Placement
stories.b: Leapmotor got official approval to raise 6.744 billion yuan in a private placement of shares. This means the company sells new ownership units directly to specific investors like China FAW instead of the open market. A private placement is a way for a business to collect fresh money without offering its assets to everyone. The China Securities Regulatory Commission gave the green light for the transaction.
stories.i: Leapmotor received regulatory approval from the CSRC for a 6.744 billion yuan private placement involving China FAW and other investors. This mechanism allows listed entities to issue new equity privately to institutional backers. The capital injection expands the firm's balance sheet without a public offering. The regulatory clearance permits the targeted share sale to proceed.
stories.a: The China Securities Regulatory Commission granted Leapmotor clearance for a 6.744 billion yuan private placement targeted at strategic investors including China FAW. This transaction execution bypasses public markets to concentrate share issuance within an approved institutional cohort. The placement alters the capital structure and ownership concentration metrics of the firm. The regulatory sign-off finalises the structural parameters of the funding round.

stories.t: H World Group Finances Bond Offering
stories.b: H World Group finished selling a bond offering worth 3.35 billion yuan. A bond is a loan where an investor gives money to an organisation in exchange for regular interest payments until the debt is paid back. Companies use bond sales to borrow large sums of money from the public or financial institutions. The transaction successfully wrapped up for the hospitality company.
stories.i: H World Group completed a 3.35 billion yuan bond offering. Corporations use this debt instrument to borrow capital from fixed-income markets by promising regular coupon payments and principal return at maturity. The successful placement increases corporate debt obligations while providing immediate liquidity. The transaction closed with the full target amount secured.
stories.a: H World Group closed its 3.35 billion yuan debt issuance. The corporate bond placement expands the issuer's total liabilities on the balance sheet while securing long-term capital from institutional fixed-income allocators. The finalisation of the offering confirms the market-clearing yield required by debt investors. The transaction details mark the conclusion of the capital-raising exercise.

politics.b: China's National Development and Reform Commission picked 36 projects to attract 15.6 billion yuan in private capital. This effort aims to support private investment in the economy. The government agency pushes these schemes forward.
politics.i: The NDRC advanced efforts to stabilise private investment by opening 36 projects to 15.6 billion yuan in private capital. This state-backed initiative directs non-state funding into designated infrastructure and industrial ventures. The planning agency oversees the allocation.
politics.a: The NDRC selected 36 projects designed to capture 15.6 billion yuan in private capital to stabilise private investment growth. This state-directed coordination mechanism channels private liquidity into targeted public-private initiatives. The planning body manages the project pipeline.

timeline: 16 Sep
Leapmotor secured CSRC approval for a 6.744 billion yuan private placement.
16 Sep
H World Group completed a 3.35 billion yuan bond offering.

India.label: India
India.sub: Rupee drops and equities rebound as RBI holds auctions

stories.t: Indian equity indices bounce back as Sensex and Nifty register gains
stories.b: The stock market went up today because people bought shares that looked cheap after earlier falls. The Sensex index went up by nearly 333 points. The Nifty index finished the session above 23,200. An index is a group of company shares tracked together to show how a market is doing.
stories.i: Equities rebounded as investors engaged in value buying across domestic sectors. The Sensex climbed nearly 333 points by the closing bell. The Nifty index finished above 23,200.
stories.a: Equities staged a recovery driven by opportunistic carry-neutral value accumulation. The Sensex advanced nearly 333 points while the Nifty cleared 23,200. This retracement follows recent downside pressure across major benchmarks.

stories.t: Indian rupee weakens against the US dollar
stories.b: The Indian currency lost value against the US dollar. The rupee dropped by 7 paise to settle at 95.95 against the dollar. Another report noted a fall of 38 paise to 95.92.
stories.i: The Indian rupee lost ground against the US dollar during the session. The currency dropped 7 paise to settle at 95.95. A separate report documented a wider fall of 38 paise to 95.92.
stories.a: The Indian rupee depreciated against the US dollar, settling down 7 paise at 95.95. Intermittent prints captured a separate intraday low reflecting a 38 paise decline to 95.92. Spot FX desks cited sustained dollar demand weighing on domestic currency pairs.

stories.t: Reserve Bank of India announces bond conversion and liquidity auctions
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India scheduled a conversion auction for government securities worth ₹30,000 crore. The central bank — which is the main bank that runs the country's money system — also announced a variable rate reverse repo auction for ₹3,00,000 crore. Treasury bill auctions raised funds across 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day tenors.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India announced a government security conversion auction targeting an aggregate ₹30,000 crore face value. The central bank scheduled an overnight variable rate reverse repo auction for ₹3,00,000 crore under the liquidity adjustment facility. Treasury bill auctions for 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day maturities closed with yields of 5.2801%, 5.7500%, and 6.0386% respectively.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India initiated a ₹30,000 crore face value government securities conversion switch auction. Concurrently, liquidity management operations featured a ₹3,00,000 crore overnight variable rate reverse repo tender under the liquidity adjustment facility. Primary issuance results for 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day treasury bills cleared at uniform yields of 5.2801%, 5.7500%, and 6.0386% respectively.

politics.b: The Reserve Bank of India managed short-term money supplies and government debt levels through various auctions. Sovereign gold bond premature redemption dates were fixed by the central bank. Markets reacted to global economic updates from abroad.
politics.i: Central bank operations dominated domestic financial administration through liquidity management and debt switches. The Reserve Bank of India set terms for sovereign gold bond premature redemptions alongside regular bill auctions. Currency and equity movements responded to external monetary shifts.
politics.a: Monetary administration centered on Reserve Bank of India debt restructuring and liquidity sterilization operations. Sovereign gold bond redemption schedules proceeded alongside primary sovereign debt auctions. External rate expectations transmitted directly into domestic foreign exchange and equity valuations.

timeline: The Reserve Bank of India announced a government securities conversion auction for ₹30,000 crore.
Treasury bill auctions for 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day tenors concluded with accepted bids.
The Indian rupee settled lower against the US dollar at 95.95.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras awards multiple supplier and sales contracts

stories.b: A company named Vallourec won a big pipe deal for an offshore project called Sepia 2. Petrobras is the firm buying these supplies. Another company named Strohm also won a contract to supply pipe technology for pre-salt work. Pipes help move oil from deep under the sea.
stories.i: Vallourec secured a major seamless pipe contract for the Sepia 2 pre-salt project via Subsea7. Petrobras also awarded Strohm a new thermoplastic composite pipe contract. These agreements support deepwater extraction operations in Brazil.
stories.a: Vallourec captured the seamless pipe package for the Sepia 2 development through Subsea7, reinforcing its position in deepwater infrastructure. Petrobras concurrently contracted Strohm for thermoplastic composite pipe technology. Both awards underscore the ongoing capital expenditure cycle targeting pre-salt hydrocarbon reserves.

stories.b: Petrobras signed a 20-year deal to sell liquid gas to Sempra Infrastructure. Camorim started a service worth $230m to help Petrobras. These deals connect the Brazilian firm with partners in other countries.
stories.i: Sempra Infrastructure signed a 20-year liquefied natural gas sales agreement with Petrobras, supporting the Port Arthur Phase 2 project. Camorim also initiated a $230m service contract for Petrobras operations. These pacts expand the state-controlled producer's commercial footprint.
stories.a: Sempra Infrastructure anchored Port Arthur Phase 2 by executing a 20-year offtake and sales agreement with Petrobras. Camorim concurrently mobilized a $230m marine service deployment for the state-backed operator. These commercial milestones integrate Brazilian production capacity further into North American energy logistics.

politics.b: The government controls Petrobras, which makes large decisions that affect the national economy. Recent supplier deals show how state energy projects drive local business activity. Leaders watch these contracts closely because oil wealth funds public services.
politics.i: State control over Petrobras places political focus on its capital expenditure allocation and local supply chain awards. Government officials monitor multi-million dollar pre-salt contracts as indicators of industrial policy success. Energy revenue generation remains a key fiscal pillar for federal administration planning.
politics.a: State ownership of Petrobras imbues every procurement cycle and international offtake agreement with sovereign strategic weight. The administration leverages domestic supplier mandates to satisfy industrial policy objectives while extracting rents from pre-salt extraction. Consequently, capital deployment into projects like Sepia 2 functions as both a corporate investment and a macroeconomic lever.

timeline: 16 Sep
Vallourec secures a pipe contract for the Sepia 2 project

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Saudi economic growth and corporate earnings updates

stories.b: Saudi non-oil activity grew for 22 consecutive quarters. This happened even while conflict continued in the region. State-backed energy producer Saudi Aramco also led global rankings for second-quarter dividend payouts. Dividends are cash payments companies give to their shareholders as a share of profit.
stories.i: Saudi non-oil activity expanded for the 22nd quarter amid ongoing regional conflict. Saudi Aramco secured the top spot in global Q2 dividend rankings. State income remains heavily supported by corporate distributions from major energy assets.
stories.a: Non-oil activity extended its expansion streak to 22 quarters despite geopolitical friction. Saudi Aramco captured the leading position in global Q2 dividend distributions, underpinning domestic liquidity. These cash flows insulate headline metrics from broader hydrocarbon volatility.

stories.b: The OPEC Fund approved $645 million in new financing for 14 countries. Yemeni Houthi forces simultaneously claimed missile and drone attacks targeting a Saudi Aramco facility in Yanbu and the Khamis Mushait airbase. Missiles are flying weapons steered toward targets.
stories.i: The OPEC Fund approved $645 million in new financing across 14 countries. Meanwhile, Yemen's Houthis claimed ballistic missile and drone strikes against a Saudi Aramco facility in Yanbu, Khamis Mushait airbase, and King Khalid Air Base. Security incidents tested critical infrastructure defense corridors.
stories.a: The OPEC Fund cleared $645 million in fresh financing for 14 developing nations. Concurrently, Houthi forces executed coordinated ballistic missile and drone strikes targeting Saudi Aramco's Yanbu installation, Khamis Mushait airbase, and King Khalid Air Base. These kinetic disruptions test the resilience parameters of key energy export hubs.

politics.b: Yemeni Houthi forces claimed attacks on Saudi sites including an Aramco facility and airbases. The OPEC Fund also approved money for international projects.
politics.i: Houthi forces claimed multiple missile and drone strikes on Saudi Aramco infrastructure and military airbases. The OPEC Fund allocated financing packages for various international recipients.
politics.a: Cross-border kinetic strikes by Houthi forces targeted energy and military installations at Yanbu and Khamis Mushait. The OPEC Fund managed external multilateral financing approvals across 14 recipient nations.

timeline: OPEC Fund approved $645 million in new financing for 14 countries.
Yemeni Houthi forces claimed drone and missile attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities and airbases.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Nigeria inflation slows to 15.39% while currency slides

stories.b: The rate at which prices go up in Nigeria is called inflation. This rate dropped to 15.39% in August. The cost of eating and buying food stayed high at 19.57%.
stories.i: Headline inflation slowed to 15.39% in August. Food inflation remained elevated at 19.57%.
stories.a: August headline inflation printed at 15.39%. Food inflation persisted at 19.57%.

stories.b: The Nigerian naira is the official money used in the country. It lost a little bit of value against the United States dollar. The exchange rate moved to N1,329.50 per dollar at the official market.
stories.i: The naira depreciated marginally against the US dollar. The official foreign exchange window recorded a rate of N1,329.50 per dollar at NAFEM.
stories.a: The official exchange rate weakened to N1,329.50 per dollar at NAFEM. Trading sessions continue to reflect slight downward pressure on the local currency.

politics.b: Politicians discussed future gasoline prices and criticized economic plans. Regulatory groups warned citizens about fraudulent investment advertisements.
politics.i: Political figures debated potential future fuel prices under hypothetical leadership outcomes. Meanwhile, advertising regulators issued warnings regarding fraudulent AI-generated investment scams on social media platforms.
politics.a: Opposition figures projected extreme future fuel price trajectories tied to electoral outcomes. Regulatory bodies concurrently targeted synthetic media investment scams circulating on digital platforms.

Arcon warns the public about fake AI investment ads on Facebook.
16 Sep
Data shows Nigerian inflation slowed to 15.39% in August.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: Australian shares edge higher ahead of central bank decisions

stories.t: Australian Shares Gain Marginal Ground While Traders Await US Rates
stories.b: The Australian share market is the collection of shares available to buy in Australia. It rose by 0.28% on the day. Investors were waiting for the Federal Reserve, which is the central bank of the United States that sets borrowing costs. Traders held back large bets before that announcement.
stories.i: The benchmark Australian stock index crept up by 0.28%. Market participants adopted a cautious stance. Everyone awaited the upcoming Federal Reserve policy decision. Trading volumes reflected hesitation ahead of the overseas rate verdict.
stories.a: The domestic equities index eked out a 0.28% gain. Market participants remained largely sidelined. Price action stayed compressed while desks awaited the Federal Open Market Committee rate decision. The implied volatility profile suggests positioning was heavily hedged into the central bank announcement.

politics.b: There is no political news today.
politics.i: No political updates are available today.
politics.a: No political developments are reported in the current data.

timeline: The Australian stock market rose by 0.28% while traders awaited a decision from the Federal Reserve.
